title: Upgrade agent-mail-monitor into full agent-mail plugin (v1)
description:
## Goal
Grow the single-purpose agent-mail-monitor plugin into a full agent-mail plugin (monitors + skills + agent) mirroring the am CLI seam, so any agent in a plugin-enabled repo is zero-to-productive on Agent Mail. Value = onboarding + host monitors + encoded discipline ON TOP of the MCP tools, never re-wrapping them.

## Non-goals
Re-implementing am MCP tools as skills. Autonomous send/ack by an agent (v1 triage is read-and-recommend only). Re-implementing am itself — the Deno layer is a THIN wrapper (am is the capability CLI).

## Stack (decided)
Deno 2.x + strict TS + Commander + Zod + Agent-Skills SKILL.md; Deno.Command with argv (no shell); shipped as .ts via `deno run` (not compiled). Scope = "wrapper + introspection": doctor/capabilities/schema subcommands emit versioned JSON envelopes. Deferred blueprint pieces + escalation triggers: vault design/agent-mail-plugin-deferrals.md. Rationale source: raw/gpt-pi-skills-cli.md.

## Success Criteria
Rename landed with marketplace renames map; scripts ported to the Deno stack; product multi-project watch mode; doctor catches the silent registration gap; capabilities/schema introspection; onboard/product-setup/coordinate skills (decision-procedure style, with routing evals); read-only mail-triage agent; plugin validates; deno fmt/lint/check + tests pass; installs migrate cleanly.
close_reason: v1 shipped: read-only Agent Mail plugin landed on main (a8059bd, pushed) and live at 0.4.0/project/enabled. All 10 children closed — CLI (watch/product/monitor/doctor/capabilities/schema), product mode, mail-triage agent, and 5 skills (onboarding-to-agent-mail, wiring-a-product-bus, toggle, doctor, driving-swarms-with-mail). id kept agent-mail-monitor (displayName 'Agent Mail', no rename) per .1. Follow-ups tracked outside the epic: manual monitor re-arm deferred (no live identity this session); human-only rm of superseded scripts/{mail-monitor,watch-mail}.sh.

title: Rebrand plugin surface to "Agent Mail" (displayName/description), keep id agent-mail-monitor
description:
## Goal
Present the plugin as the fuller **"Agent Mail"** product (monitors + skills +
read-only triage agent) **without renaming the plugin id**. The id
`agent-mail-monitor` is load-bearing for installs — a consumer's `enabledPlugins`
keys on `<id>@marketplace`, skill namespaces are `<id>:skill`, and the plugin
cache dir is `<id>/<version>/` — so changing it silently disables the plugin for
anyone who installed it. Only the **presentational** surface changes.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change plugin.json `name` (the id) — that is the breakage this bead
  deliberately avoids. Decision recorded 2026-07-24: consumers already installed
  `agent-mail-monitor`; keep the id.
- No `renames` map — unnecessary when the id is unchanged (it exists only to
  migrate an id rename, which we are not doing).

## Acceptance Criteria
- marketplace.json entry: `displayName` "Agent Mail Monitor" -> "Agent Mail";
  `description` broadened to cover monitors + skills + read-only triage agent
  (not just the monitor).
- plugin.json `description` broadened to match; `name` UNCHANGED
  (`agent-mail-monitor`).
- version bump plugin.json -> 0.4.0 (feature growth).
- README / docs framing updated to the "Agent Mail" product where the reference
  is presentational; the id `agent-mail-monitor` retained in skill namespaces,
  cache paths, and script echo strings.
- `claude plugin validate .` passes.

## Verification
- `claude plugin validate .` passes.
- `jq -r .name plugins/agent-mail-monitor/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` == `agent-mail-monitor` (unchanged).
- `jq -r '.plugins[0].displayName' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json` == `Agent Mail`.
- The existing `enabledPlugins` key `agent-mail-monitor@tiny-claude-plugins`
  still resolves — no id change, so no consumer re-enable needed.
close_reason: Rebrand landed in 49cc0d8: displayName -> Agent Mail, broadened descriptions, version 0.4.0, id agent-mail-monitor unchanged (no renames map). claude plugin validate passed.

title: Reconsider 'coordinate' skill: boundary leak + loaded verb vs Agent Mail scope
description:
## Goal
Decide whether the `coordinate` skill (landed in tcp-6yk.6) belongs in this
plugin at all, and if so under what name — before v1 ships (tcp-6yk.8).

## Background
The plugin's identity is **Agent Mail**: monitor inboxes, query mail, triage
mail. The `coordinate` skill instead teaches the *whole* shared-tree swarm loop
(reserve -> announce -> work -> commit --only -> release -> close). Two concerns:

1. **Domain/boundary leak.** Swarm coordination is a broader workflow than Agent
   Mail. It *uses* AM's file-reservation + messaging primitives, but the skill
   also covers git commit discipline, bead lifecycle, and build slots — none of
   which are AM. A user installing an "Agent Mail" plugin does not expect a
   general swarm-coordination playbook to ride along.
2. **Loaded verb.** "coordinate" is generic and overloaded; it reads as a
   top-level capability claim rather than "the mail-driven slice of coordination."

## Non-goals
- Not re-litigating whether the swarm loop is *useful* (it is) — only whether it
  belongs under the Agent Mail plugin's namespace/identity.
- No behavior change to the watch/query/triage code.

## Options to weigh
- **Keep + rename** to something scoped to the mail seam (e.g. `mail-driven-swarm`
  / `reserve-and-announce`) so the name doesn't overclaim.
- **Narrow the skill** to only the AM-native primitives (reservations + threads),
  cross-linking out to the broader swarm rules rather than restating git/beads.
- **Relocate** the skill to a coordination-focused plugin/home and drop it here.
- **Keep as-is** if we decide AM's reservation/messaging seam legitimately anchors
  the whole loop for this audience.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A decision recorded (keep-as-is / rename / narrow / relocate) with a one-line
  rationale, reconciled against the plugin's stated scope in plugin.json +
  marketplace.json description.
- If rename/narrow/relocate: the change applied (skill dir + any SKILL.md refs +
  disable-model-invocation intact) and re-validated with skill-check.
- v1 ships (tcp-6yk.8) consistent with the decision — no dangling "coordinate"
  name if we chose to rename.

## Verification
- `skill-check check <skill-dir> --strict --no-security-scan` PASS after any edit.
- plugin description and skill set read as coherent (no scope overclaim) on a
  fresh read of marketplace.json + the skills/ listing.
close_reason: Renamed skills/coordinate → driving-swarms-with-mail (gerund form, matching the skill-naming convention); description re-anchored on the Agent Mail reservation/thread seam, git/tracker steps demoted to generic hygiene. skill-check --strict PASS (100/100).

title: plan-to-beads: add reconcile mode for already-beadified plans (greenfield-assumption fix)
description:
## Goal

Add a **reconcile mode** to the `plan-to-beads` skill
(`.claude/skills/plan-to-beads/SKILL.md`) so that running it against a plan whose
beads **already exist** updates the existing graph instead of duplicating it. The
skill's current flow assumes greenfield: its execution step runs
`author_beads.py --execute`, which is non-idempotent and *creates* beads, so a
re-beadify (or a plan written from pre-existing beads) yields a duplicate graph.

Evidence + design: `design/plan-to-beads-reconcile-mode.md` (this run against
epic `tcp-6yk`, where all 10 beads pre-existed).

## Non-goals

- Making `author_beads.py --execute` itself idempotent (upsert-by-key) — larger
  change; the detection-gate branch is the cheaper, sufficient fix for now.
- Removing the greenfield path — keep `author_beads.py` for genuinely new graphs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SKILL.md` gains a **Step 0 / detection gate**: query the id prefix
  (`br list --json | jq 'select(.id|startswith("<prefix>"))'`) BEFORE the
  author/dry-run steps; if beads for this plan already exist, branch to reconcile
  mode rather than `--execute`.
- Reconcile mode documents the three moves proven this run: (1) self-containment +
  drift check via `br show` → `br update --title/--description`; (2) add the
  missing `blocks` edges that gate the frontier (parent-child does NOT gate);
  (3) verify with `br ready` + `bv --robot-triage --graph-root <epic>`.
- The `bv` output-path gotcha is recorded in `references/br-bv-mechanics.md`:
  v0.18.0 nests under a top-level `triage` key
  (`.triage.project_health.graph.has_cycles`); a bare `.project_health.…` path
  returns `null`, which must not be misread as "no cycles".

## Verification

- Re-running `plan-to-beads` on an already-beadified plan hits the detection gate
  and does not create duplicate ids (`wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl` unchanged by a
  reconcile pass except for edge/field updates).
- Grep `SKILL.md` for the Step 0 gate and the reconcile-mode block.
- `references/br-bv-mechanics.md` contains the `triage`-key path note.

title: agent-mail message <global-id> — cross-project message lookup in one command
description:
## Goal Add a coordinator-facing, read-only `agent-mail message ` command that resolves an Agent Mail message by its server-wide-unique id across projects — in ONE command, with no project guessing. This is the headline of the epic: it addresses the exact friction a cross-repo coordinator hits. ## Background Agent Mail message ids are globally unique, but the read path is project-scoped: `am robot message ` requires `--project` (falls back to CWD) and returns "message # not found" when pointed at the wrong project. `am robot overview` is cross-project but returns only per-project counts, not a message. So there is no single `am` command mapping a bare id to its message. Verified this turn: finding #27588 required trying `tiny-claude-plugins` (not found) then the vault (found). ## Design sketch - New subcommand in the Deno CLI: `agent-mail message [--product ]`. - Resolution strategy: enumerate candidate projects via `am robot projects --json` (or, when `--product`/$AGENT_MAIL_PRODUCT is set, the product-linked projects only), then probe `am robot message --project

` until one resolves; return it (project + message). - Read-only; emits the same versioned JSON envelope as the other query commands (`--json`), plus a human view. - Bound the fan-out (log if projects are skipped); short-circuit on first hit. ## Constraints - Read-only by construction — no mutation tools. - Reuse the existing envelope/exit-code contract (introspect.ts / envelope.ts). - Prefer a real `am` global primitive if one is added upstream; until then, wrap the fan-out. ## Acceptance Criteria - `agent-mail message 27588` (no project flag) returns the message + its project in one invocation from any cwd. - `--product ` scopes the search to product-linked projects. - Not-found across all candidates yields a clear, single diagnostic (not N stacked errors) and a non-zero exit per the contract. - `--json` emits a valid versioned envelope; a test covers hit + miss. ## Verification `deno test --allow-write` covers a resolved id and an unresolved id; `deno check` and `skill-check` (if a skill references it) stay green.

title: diagnose-agent-mail-service skill: recognize server-wedge signature + correct probe ordering
description:
## Goal
A `diagnose-agent-mail-service` skill (agent-mail-monitor plugin) that correctly diagnoses a
suspected Agent Mail **server wedge** — HTTP unresponsive while the process is still running —
using the right tool ordering and routing to recovery, without misreading the signature.

## Background
2026-07-24 incident (HazyRiver + WindyBarn): `am status` hung (10s timeout) while `:8765`
stayed bound. A first snapshot misdiagnosed this as *"unit inactive, orphan process holds the
port."* Ground truth: the systemd unit was `active (running)` and the port-holder **was** its
Main PID — a **wedged-but-alive** server, not a dead unit. The misdiagnosis came from probing
with the wrong tools.

Verified tool split (this is the skill's core knowledge):

| Command | Path | When server is wedged |
|---|---|---|
| `am status` | **HTTP** → server | **hangs** — it IS the symptom, never use it as the probe |
| `am robot status` / `robot inbox` | **local sqlite** | return **instantly** — safe reads |
| `am robot atc` | local sqlite | on this build returns `"enabled": false` (`AM_ATC_ENABLED=false`) — **not** a health surface |
| `systemctl --user status mcp-agent-mail.service` | systemd | **authoritative**: managed? alive? Main PID? — beats `ss`/`pgrep`, which cannot tell managed-vs-orphan |

Root cause of the wedge was environmental: connection leak (`drop_close` on storage.sqlite3) +
memory/swap pressure + a **corrupt archive git repo** (`~/.mcp_agent_mail_git_mailbox_repo`,
`git fsck` = empty objects) failing maintenance every tick.

## Non-goals
- Not an `am` source change; the CLI already has the pieces — the skill ties them into a playbook.
- Does not auto-restart or auto-repair; it diagnoses and recommends (restart / archive-repair are
  mutations the operator confirms).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Skill recognizes the **"port bound + `am status` hangs"** signature and names it a wedge, not
  a dead unit.
- Probe ordering is **systemctl-first → `am robot status` (local read) → HTTP last**, and it
  explicitly warns NOT to diagnose with `am status` (the hanging call).
- It names the recovery: `systemctl --user restart mcp-agent-mail.service` (clean because the
  port-holder is the Main PID → no orphan/EADDRINUSE), and flags corrupt-archive as a **separate,
  human-run** repair (empty-object cleanup is `find -delete`/`rm` under `/home`).
- `skill-check check <dir> --strict --no-security-scan` → 0 errors.

## Verification
Run the skill against the currently-healthy server → it reports healthy via the local-DB read and
a fast HTTP probe. The documented recipe reproduces the 2026-07-24 incident's correct diagnosis
(wedged-alive, restart clears it, archive repair separate).

## Notes
Pairs with the systemd health-watchdog bead (the durable "ensure service" companion). The skill
is the human-in-the-loop diagnosis; the watchdog is the unattended auto-recovery.
close_reason: Built diagnose-agent-mail-service skill (SKILL.md + scripts/diagnose.sh + resources/recovery.md). skill-check 100/100, 0 errors. Happy-path + WEDGED/agent-skip/usage negative tests pass. NOTE: live re-probing corrected two details from this bead's original sketch — the wedge-safe local read is 'am robot inbox' (~0.15s), NOT 'robot status' (which aliases the slow 1.3-15.8s 'am status' synthesis and would false-positive a wedge); the decisive fast probe is curl to /mcp/ (any code=alive, 000=wedged).

title: systemd health-watchdog for mcp-agent-mail: liveness-based restart (Restart=on-failure can't catch a wedged-alive process)
description:
## Goal
Make the `mcp-agent-mail` systemd user service self-recover from a **wedged-but-alive** state
(HTTP unresponsive while the process keeps running) — the failure mode the current
`Restart=on-failure` cannot catch — plus add a memory guardrail.

## Background
The unit (`~/.config/systemd/user/mcp-agent-mail.service`) already has `Restart=on-failure` +
`RestartSec=3`. But a hung-alive process never exits or signals failure, so systemd sees it as
healthy and **never restarts it** — which is exactly why the 2026-07-24 wedge persisted for days
(uptime since 2026-07-17). `Restart=on-failure` is liveness-blind; we need a **health**-based
restart. Memory pressure was also present (peak 826M, swap 292M), and an unclean write under that
pressure is the likely origin of the corrupt archive git repo.

## Design sketch (confirm the two open questions first)
- **Open Q1:** does `mcp-agent-mail serve` expose an HTTP health endpoint (e.g. `/health` on
  127.0.0.1:8765)? **Open Q2:** does the binary `sd_notify(WATCHDOG=1)`?
- **If Q2 yes →** native `WatchdogSec=` in the unit (simplest, in-process liveness).
- **If Q2 no (build-agnostic, default plan) →** a `mcp-agent-mail-health.timer` + oneshot
  `mcp-agent-mail-health.service` that probes the **HTTP path** — `timeout 6 am status`, or
  `curl -fsS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8765/health` if the endpoint exists — and runs
  `systemctl --user restart mcp-agent-mail.service` after N consecutive failures.
  - ⚠ The probe MUST hit HTTP. `am robot status` reads local sqlite and returns fine *through*
    a wedge, so it would hide the very failure we're detecting.
- **Memory guardrail:** `MemoryHigh=`/`MemoryMax=` + `OOMPolicy=` so runaway memory forces a
  clean restart instead of silent degradation (and stops the unclean-write → corrupt-archive cycle).
- **Archive hygiene:** one-time repair of `~/.mcp_agent_mail_git_mailbox_repo` (remove empty
  objects, `git fsck`, re-init if needed); optionally an `ExecStartPre=` fsck guard.

## Non-goals
- No change to the app binary; this is unit/timer + ops config only.
- Not removing `Restart=on-failure` — it stays for the crash case; the watchdog adds the
  wedge/liveness case it can't cover.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A wedged-but-alive server (HTTP unresponsive) is auto-restarted within a bounded window.
- A healthy server is never needlessly restarted (probe hits HTTP, tolerates N transient misses).
- A memory cap is in place with a defined OOM policy.
- The two open questions (health endpoint? sd_notify?) are answered and the chosen mechanism
  (native watchdog vs timer-probe) is recorded.

## Verification
Induce or await a wedge → the watchdog restarts the service within the probe interval;
`systemctl --user show mcp-agent-mail.service -p NRestarts` increments and `am status` (HTTP)
responds again without manual intervention. Under a synthetic memory balloon, the cgroup cap
trips the configured OOM policy rather than swapping indefinitely.

## Notes
Companion to the `diagnose-agent-mail-service` skill bead (human-in-loop diagnosis ↔ unattended
auto-recovery). This is machine infra (systemd user units), not plugin code — tracked here with
the diagnosis skill so the pair stays discoverable; may re-home if a better tracker fits.
close_reason: ELEGANT DECISION (2026-07-24): do NOT build a bespoke liveness-watchdog (health.timer + probe service). Live investigation showed the server already SELF-HEALS on restart — its startup integrity probe detected archive-ahead-of-DB + sqlite corruption and auto-recovered (recovered ~19 projects/6 messages from the archive; git fsck now exits 0; archive maintenance completes clean). The reason Restart=on-failure 'could not catch the wedge' is that a memory-bloated-but-alive process never EXITS. Fix: applied MemoryHigh=1200M/MemoryMax=1536M live+persistent via 'systemctl --user set-property' (drop-ins under ~/.config/systemd/user.control/). Runaway memory -> hard cap -> OOM-kill -> clean exit -> existing Restart=on-failure -> startup auto-recovery. One property turns the uncatchable wedge into an already-handled crash; zero new infra. Detection side is covered by the diagnose-agent-mail-service skill (tcp-p0x.10). If a CONFIRMED curl-000 wedge (not slow am status) ever recurs without a memory cause, reopen for a health.timer then — YAGNI until then. ALSO resolves the manual archive-repair follow-up: already self-healed by the 22:18 restart (fsck exit 0; the 1 remaining empty object is unreferenced/harmless).

title: monitor: single-project watch recovery silently drops messages read-elsewhere during a poll outage (transport hole)
description:
## Goal
Make the single-project mail watch's recovery lossless: a message that arrives
during a `check-inbox` poll outage must still produce a notification even if it is
marked read (by another session's fetch/ack) before the watch recovers.

## Background
The watch keeps an id high-water mark (`last`) across failed polls and, on
recovery, re-emits messages from the latest `check-inbox` payload whose id exceeds
`last`. But `am check-inbox` returns **unread messages only**. So a message that
(a) arrives while polling is failing, then (b) is read elsewhere before the watch
recovers, has already left the unread set — recovery cannot see it, and it is
silently dropped. No error, no notification.

This is the root cause that compounded the 27635 miss: the monitor snapshot showed
`check-inbox` failing 3× ("did not return JSON") then "recovered", but recovery
over an unread-only source cannot replay what left the set during the outage. It is
distinct from the scope gap (watching only one project) tracked separately — this
bug bites even when the message lands in the correctly-armed project.

The product-scoped watch does NOT have this hole: it uses `am products inbox
--since-ts <ts>`, a server-side since-fetch that returns messages regardless of
read state. The fix here brings single-project mode up to the same recovery
guarantee (or routes single-project recovery through a since-timestamped read).

## Non-goals
- No change to the product-scoped watch (already lossless via `--since-ts`).
- No new mutation surface — the watch stays read-only (never marks messages read).
- Not the cross-project scope fix (separate work); this is recovery correctness
  within one project.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Arm the single-project watch for identity A in project P.
2. Induce a poll outage (e.g. server wedge / `check-inbox` returning non-JSON for
   several ticks).
3. During the outage, send A a message in P, then have another session fetch/ack
   it (marking it read) before the watch recovers.
4. On recovery the watch emits nothing for that message — it is gone from the
   unread set. Silent loss.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After a poll outage, a message that arrived during the outage and was read
  elsewhere still produces exactly one notification on recovery (no silent drop).
- The recovery path reads by a since-watermark that is independent of read state
  (e.g. a `--since-ts`-style fetch), not the unread-only `check-inbox` set.
- No duplicate notifications for messages already emitted before the outage.
- Still read-only: recovery never marks a message read.
- A test reproduces "arrived-during-outage, read-elsewhere, still notified".

## Verification
`deno test --allow-write` covers the outage-then-read-elsewhere recovery path;
`deno check` stays green. Manually reproduce the four-step scenario and confirm one
notification lands on recovery.

title: product-scoped watch: group repos by workload not human + work-descriptive product-key naming (privacy)
description:
## Goal
Establish the convention for grouping an operator's repos into an Agent Mail
product for the product-scoped watch: group by **workload (repos)**, never by
**human**, and give the product a **work-descriptive** key. This keeps the
cross-project subscription privacy-clean and prevents re-introducing operator
identity-exposure through the grouping.

## Background
The product-scoped watch (sibling work) needs a product that links the operator's
active project-keys. The tempting shortcut — a durable record mapping one human to
their N agent identities ("operator roster") — is exactly the identity-exposure
move flagged in this vault: it materializes, in durable state, that N agent
identities are all one person.

Prior art (SPIFFE, W3C did:wba, Microsoft Entra) converges on: identity is
workload-scoped (SPIFFE trust domain ≈ AM `project_key`), and the human stays
*above* the identity graph, never a node in it (did:wba: the human never becomes
the DID). An AM product groups **repos**, not people, so it is the privacy-safe
primitive — provided its key names the *work*, not the operator.

The only leak vector is the product key's name: `gulp-repos` / an email / a handle
re-imports the exposure; `everything-ecosystem` (or similar work descriptor) stays
workload-scoped. This mirrors the discipline AM already enforces on agent names
(identity/role-descriptive names rejected in favour of a random adjective+noun).

## Non-goals
- No `roster.jsonl` / operator entity — explicitly do NOT build it (overbuilt and
  an exposure surface). If a multi-crew gap survives identity convergence, escalate
  toward AM's own product / `am service` primitives, not a hand-rolled file.
- No change to how agent identities are minted (that is the identity-convergence
  bead).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented rule (in the plugin's product-watch docs / onboarding) that a
  product key MUST be work-descriptive and MUST NOT encode the operator (no
  human name, email, or handle).
- The product-watch setup guidance groups by project-key (workload), and nowhere
  records a human→identities mapping.
- The rationale cites the workload-scoping principle (why grouping by repos, not by
  human, is both sufficient and privacy-preserving).

## Verification
Review the product-watch setup docs: the naming rule is stated, the example key is
work-descriptive, and no artifact links agent identities to a human. A reviewer can
point to the rule and the SPIFFE/did:wba rationale.

title: monitor: swap watch backend to append-only canonical git-mailbox (retire check-inbox from the notification path)
description:
## Goal

Replace the mail watch's notification backend: read new mail from the **append-only
canonical git-mailbox on disk** (already implemented as the shadow's `snapshotMailbox`
in `src/core/mailbox.ts`), watermark by message id, and **remove `am check-inbox`
from the notification path**. This is a genuinely read-only backend and it dissolves
three separately-filed failure modes at once.

## Background

**Verdict (source-verified against am v0.3.21):** `am check-inbox` is **not
read-only when the am daemon is up (the default)**. Without `--direct` it
unconditionally takes the daemon/HTTP path
(`check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct=false, *) → true`, lib.rs:7250 + tests at
lib.rs:37108) and invokes the server's **consuming `fetch_inbox`** MCP tool, whose
contract is literally "Retrieve recent messages … and mark returned messages read"
(messaging.rs:3106 → `apply_auto_read_timestamp`, :3358). The genuinely read-only
SELECT path (`check_inbox_direct` → `fetch_inbox_metadata_rows_from_conn`,
lib.rs:71126) is reachable ONLY with `--direct` AND no daemon listening. The
plugin's `pollInbox` passes no `--direct`, and a daemon is normally live — so
**every poll consumes**, marking mail read and stealing it from a later interactive
`fetch_inbox(unread_only)`.

**One root cause, three symptoms.** The watch trusts mutable/consumable SQLite
read-state (via check-inbox) as source of truth instead of the append-only
canonical git-mailbox:
1. **Consuming** — this verdict (the poll marks mail read).
2. **DB-desync blind spot** — when SQLite under-represents the canonical archive,
   `check-inbox` returns `rows_returned:0` while real mail sits on disk → false
   silence (see the desync incident, msg 27647).
3. **Transport hole** — `tcp-p0x.12`: unread-only recovery loses a message marked
   read elsewhere during a poll outage.

All three vanish if the watch reads the canonical store and watermarks by id.

**The backend already exists and is dogfooded.** `src/core/mailbox.ts`
(`snapshotMailbox`) reads
`<ROOT>/projects/<slug>/agents/<Agent>/inbox/YYYY/MM/<ts>__<subject>__<id>.md`,
parses the id off the filename tail (anchored regex; regression-tested in
`src/core/mailbox_test.ts` incl. the msg-27650 `___<id>` case), and is genuinely
read-only at the OS level. The shadow command (`src/commands/shadow.ts`, part A)
already emits `MAIL #<id>` off this store and fired correctly live (msgs
27657/27660/27661). This bead promotes part A from prototype to THE watch backend.

Design writeup (vault, for context — the bead is self-contained without it):
`design/agent-mail-watch-canonical-backend.md` in the everything vault.

## Non-goals

- NOT wiring the optional doctor cross-check (shadow part B) — that is a follow-up.
  A candidate non-consuming SQLite read (`am robot inbox`) must be source-verified
  read-only first; do not assume it (a "read-only" label is exactly what proved
  false for check-inbox).
- NOT the cross-project scope work (`tcp-p0x.6`) — orthogonal; the FS reader
  already supports multiple slugs, so this composes with it later.
- NOT removing `pollInbox`/check-inbox from the codebase — the shadow experiment
  still uses it as the divergence probe; only remove it from the *notification*
  path (`watch` / `monitor`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `runWatch` (single-project `watch` + the `monitor` entrypoint) emits one line per
  NEW canonical message using `snapshotMailbox` + an id high-water mark; it no
  longer calls `pollInbox`/`am check-inbox`. Arming the watch does not mark any mail
  read (verify: `read_ts` unchanged after N polls over delivered mail).
- Baseline poll adopts the current canonical id set silently (no replay of existing
  mail); only post-launch arrivals emit. `--since <id>` still replays ids > N once.
- Missing mailbox root / unparseable files degrade loudly (a warning line), never a
  crash and never silent — reuse the shadow's `warnMissingRoot` / skipped-file
  handling.
- The private-layout coupling is guarded: a `doctor` check resolves the mailbox
  root and asserts the `<ts>__<subject>__<id>.md` layout parses (fail loud if the
  private layout shifts). Anchored parser + regression test already landed.
- `tcp-p0x.12` (transport hole) is closed as subsumed: the FS backend is
  append-only, so unread-only recovery loss cannot occur. Cross-link in the close.
- Docs/comments already retracted (monitors.json, watch-mail.sh, toggle SKILL.md,
  mail-triage.md, am.ts/mailbox.ts/shadow.ts/cli.ts) are consistent with the new
  backend.

## Verification

- `deno test src/core/mailbox_test.ts` green (parser + snapshot).
- New/updated watch test: given a temp mailbox tree, arming emits only
  post-baseline ids, watermarks monotonically, and never invokes `am`.
- Live dogfood: arm the watch as WindyBarn against the real git-mailbox root,
  send a test message, confirm the notification fires AND `am check-inbox --direct`
  (no daemon) / a direct SQLite read shows the message still UNREAD after the
  notification.

## Convergence gate (future, not this bead)

When upstream enables the Product Bus, swap the FS reader for `am products inbox
--since-ts` (a committed, non-consuming server API) and keep the FS reader as the
daemon-agnostic/offline fallback. Tracked by the vault note
`wiki/agent-mail-product-bus-worktrees-gate.md`. Caution: `am products inbox`
silently bypasses `WORKTREES_ENABLED` offline, so confirm the bus is enabled
server-side before trusting the swap.

title: monitor: show project-key (bus identity) in the notification label, not just repo basename
description:
## Goal

Surface the **Agent Mail project-key** (the `human_key` = absolute cwd path the
identity is registered under) in the monitor's notification label, so a human
watching a multi-session/multi-repo setup can tell **which bus** a notification
came from at a glance.

Today the notification renders as:

    ● Monitor event: "new Agent Mail for WindyBarn @ tiny-claude-plugins (0.4.0)"

`tiny-claude-plugins` there is the repo **basename**, not the project-key. Agent
Mail's project identity IS the absolute cwd path (a sibling repo and the vault are
different projects that can share a basename-ish label), so the basename alone
does not answer "which bus am I subscribed to". Show the project-key.

## Non-goals

- No change to the per-message stdout line (`MAIL #<id> from <sender> …` from
  `formatLine` in `src/commands/watch.ts`) — that is the delivery payload and
  stays terse.
- No new watch/transport behavior — this is a labeling/QoL change only.
- Not the cross-project *watch* feature (tcp-p0x.6) nor global message *lookup*
  (tcp-p0x.1) — this is purely how the single label identifies its bus.

## Context / investigation (2026-07-25, WindyBarn)

- The per-message notification body is `formatLine()` (`src/commands/watch.ts:27`)
  → `MAIL #<id> from <from> [<importance>]: <subject>` — it carries no project id.
- The `"new Agent Mail for <AGENT_NAME> @ <project> (<version>)"` text is the
  **monitor-event label**, not emitted by `formatLine`; grep finds it nowhere in
  the plugin source, so it is composed by the harness/monitor framing from the
  monitor `name`/`description` (`monitors/monitors.json`) + resolved env
  (`AGENT_NAME`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`) + plugin version. Confirm the exact
  emission site during implementation — it may require the plugin to emit its own
  richer startup/label line rather than relying on harness composition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The monitor notification identifies its bus by **project-key** (the absolute
  path used as the Agent Mail `human_key`), not only the repo basename — e.g.
  `… @ /home/gulp/projects/tiny-claude-plugins` (full path, or basename + full
  path), so two buses that would collide on basename are distinguishable.
- In **product / multi-project** mode the label reflects the product/bus scope
  being watched, consistent with the single-project format.
- The `AGENT_NAME`-unset idle path and the first-poll-FAILED path keep working
  (labels there already name agent + project — keep them consistent).
- No change to `formatLine`'s per-message output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch a session with `AGENT_NAME=WindyBarn` in a repo, monitor auto-arms.
2. Receive a new Agent Mail message.
3. Observe `● Monitor event: "new Agent Mail for WindyBarn @ tiny-claude-plugins
   (0.4.0)"` — the `@` segment is the basename, so with a second bus of similar
   basename you cannot tell which subscription fired.

## Verification

- Trigger a notification and confirm the label contains the full project-key.
- If product mode is exercised, confirm its label names the product/bus scope.
- `deno fmt`, `deno lint`, `deno check`, and `deno test` green in
  `plugins/agent-mail-monitor/`.

title: doctor mcp-declaration: four-state fix (handle rejected server)
description:
## Goal
Fix the doctor's `mcp-declaration` remedy so it resolves the most common real failure — a
server that is declared but REJECTED — instead of prescribing a fix that cannot work.
GrayBrook ranked this the one real bug in the review.

## Background
When the agent's MCP mail tools are missing, doctor emits
`[WARN] mcp-declaration → resources/declare-mcp.md`. That resource offers two fixes: run `am`
(auto-detects agents, refreshes MCP), or `claude mcp add --scope …`. Neither clears a prior
rejection, which persists in `.claude/settings.local.json`:
`"disabledMcpjsonServers": ["mcp-agent-mail"]`. Adding a fresh declaration on top of a
rejected one leaves it rejected — a dead end. `claude mcp get <name>` names the state outright
("Status: ✘ Rejected (see disabledMcpjsonServers in settings)").

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a project whose `.mcp.json` declares agent-mail, reject it at the approval prompt (or add
   `mcp-agent-mail` to `disabledMcpjsonServers` in `.claude/settings.local.json`).
2. Start a session; MCP mail tools are absent.
3. Run the doctor skill → `[WARN] mcp-declaration → declare-mcp.md`.
4. Follow declare-mcp.md (`am`, or `claude mcp add`). The tools remain absent; nothing the
   file prescribes removes the `disabledMcpjsonServers` entry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The mcp-declaration check runs `claude mcp get <name>` and branches on Status across four
  states, each with the correct fix:
  - absent → today's guidance (`am`, or `claude mcp add`)
  - `✘ Rejected` → remove the name from `disabledMcpjsonServers` in `.claude/settings.local.json`
  - `⏸ Pending approval` → approve at next startup / `/reload-plugins`; no config edit
  - `✔ Connected` → pass
- `declare-mcp.md` carries the four-state table.
- Secondary: replace the `grep -i agent-mail` substring match (over-matches unrelated names)
  with an exact-name check, and drop the hard `/mcp/` path assumption (verify against
  `am status --json .service.http_url`; GrayBrook's server served `/api/`).

## Verification
Reproduce the rejected state, run the patched doctor, confirm it names the rejected state and
the settings-file remedy; `/reload-plugins` brings tools up without a restart.

title: toggle ON path: fix stale mail-monitor.sh entrypoint + add mid-session identity route
description:
## Goal
Fix the `toggle` skill's "Turn it ON" path: it points at the SUPERSEDED bash entrypoint and
offers no mid-session identity route — the exact situation that sends a user to the skill.

## Background
Two defects in skills/toggle/SKILL.md "Turn it ON":
1. WRONG ENTRYPOINT. It arms `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/scripts/mail-monitor.sh`. The 0.4.0
   monitor entrypoint is the Deno CLI: `deno run --allow-run=am --allow-env --allow-read
   "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/cli.ts" monitor` (see monitors/monitors.json). `mail-monitor.sh`
   is the retired bash shim slated for removal. Confirmed live this session — arming had to
   use the Deno entrypoint, contradicting the skill.
2. NO MID-SESSION ROUTE. The ON path says only "Set one at launch: AGENT_NAME=YourName", but
   the reason you reach the toggle skill is that you are ALREADY mid-session with no identity;
   relaunching is precisely what you cannot do. The working move — prefixing the env onto the
   Monitor command — is undocumented:
   `AGENT_NAME=<name> CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<path> deno run … src/cli.ts monitor`
   (the CLI reads both from its own environment, so this arms correctly in a live session).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch a session with no AGENT_NAME.
2. Invoke the toggle skill and follow "Turn it ON".
3. It points at `scripts/mail-monitor.sh` (wrong for 0.4.0) and tells you to relaunch — which
   you cannot do mid-session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The ON path arms the 0.4.0 Deno entrypoint (`src/cli.ts monitor`), not `mail-monitor.sh`.
- It documents the mid-session env-prefix arming move (AGENT_NAME + CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR on the
  command).
- The OFF path's "find the task running mail-monitor.sh" language is updated to the Deno
  command label.
- `skill-check check skills/toggle --strict --no-security-scan` → PASS.
- Coordinate with the human-only removal of the superseded scripts/{mail-monitor,watch-mail}.sh
  so the skill and the shipped files agree.

## Verification
Re-arm from a no-identity session by following the patched skill verbatim; the monitor starts
on the Deno entrypoint and watches the given identity.
close_reason: Fixed toggle ON path: arm the 0.4.0 Deno entrypoint (deno run … src/cli.ts monitor, matching monitors.json) instead of the retired scripts/mail-monitor.sh; OFF path now IDs the task by its stable agent-mail-inbox label; corrected the 'needs jq' claim (0.4.0 monitor parses am JSON with Zod, no jq); added a mid-session identity route (AGENT_NAME=… command prefix, since a later shell export doesn't reach the running watch). skill-check 100/100 PASS.

title: identity-picking: list existing agents (am agents list -p) when AGENT_NAME unset
description:
## Goal
When AGENT_NAME is unset, help the user PICK an existing registered identity instead of
minting a new one — surfacing the project's current agents so they reuse one and avoid
orphaning reservations.

## Background
The `agent-name` check warns that AGENT_NAME is unset; `set-agent-name.md` says pick a durable
adjective+noun and use it every session. Both are correct but incomplete: a project often
already has registered identities, and the right move is to REUSE one, not mint a fourth. The
plugin's own docs warn that "a new name mints a new empty mailbox and orphans prior
reservations" — so the fix actively steers away from a failure mode the docs already name.
GrayBrook's project had three identities (GrayBrook, QuietFalcon, CrimsonMaple); the doctor
never showed them.

Note: `set-agent-name.md` uses `PlumHare` as its concrete example name. This literal leaked
into a coordinator's session notes as a phantom "real" identity that did not exist — consider
making the example obviously illustrative (or generating one) to avoid that trap.

## Constraints
- Read-only. Just list; never register on the user's behalf.
- `am agents list` currently needs `-p <path>` (a positional key is rejected) — use the flag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- When AGENT_NAME is unset, the doctor (and the onboarding skill's identity step) run
  `am agents list -p <project-key>` and print the candidate identities (name, model,
  last-active), framed as "reuse one of these, or mint a new adjective+noun".
- The doctor is the natural home — it already knows the project key.
- `set-agent-name.md`'s `PlumHare` example is made clearly illustrative (or the guidance points
  at the live list instead of a hard-coded name).

## Verification
In a project with ≥1 registered agent and no AGENT_NAME, the doctor lists the existing
identities; the onboarding step references the same list.

title: polish: exit-3 framing, health WARN probe-naming, DB-lock hint; report am positional-key upstream
description:
## Goal
Triage the polish-tier findings from GrayBrook's review — small framing/CLI clarity items, and
one upstream `am` note that is out of scope to fix here.

## Background
Lower-ranked findings from message #27588, grouped:

1. exit-3 framing. The monitor auto-arms, finds no AGENT_NAME, exits 3 — which the harness
   surfaces as `status: failed` ("script failed (exit 3)"). The stdout notice is excellent and
   loud, but "failed" reads as a crash and prompts a "was mail dropped?" check (it wasn't —
   read-only by design). If the harness allows, distinguish "idle / not armed" from "failed"
   with the same loudness minus the false alarm. Deliberate design choice — evaluate, don't
   assume a change.
2. health WARN overstates. `[WARN] health — am health: overall=unhealthy level=green` sent
   GrayBrook chasing a disagreement: `am doctor check --json` says `healthy: true`, while
   `am health` flags one probe, `archive_db_parity` (archive 152 projects vs DB 133; messages
   differ by 6 of 6223 — old sandbox eval dirs, no mail at risk). Fix: name the failing probe
   in the WARN line (`health — am health: unhealthy (probe: archive_db_parity)`); when parity
   is the only failing probe, arguably INFO, not WARN.
3. DB-lock contention on mutating ops. A mutating `am` op (contact approve / mail reply) can be
   blocked by an exclusive activity lock held by the running server; the MCP path times out
   under the same contention (observed both by GrayBrook and by the coordinator filing this).
   Consider surfacing a clearer "server busy — retry / owner pid" hint in doctor, and document
   the "verify state, don't blind-retry" discipline.

## Non-goals / upstream
- `am agents list` (and `am agents show`) rejecting a POSITIONAL project key with no hint to
  use `-p` is an upstream `am` CLI issue — report upstream, do not fix in the plugin.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Items 1–3 each either land a small plugin/doc change or are explicitly closed as
  won't-fix/deliberate with a one-line rationale.
- The `am agents list` positional-key issue is filed/reported upstream (link or note), not
  silently absorbed.

## Verification
Doctor output reflects any adopted framing/probe-naming changes; a note records the upstream
report and any deliberate no-ops.

title: monitor: cross-project / product-scoped watch (identity receives mail in multiple projects)
description:
## Goal
Let the monitor watch an identity's mail across ALL its projects (or a product's linked
projects), not just the single `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` it was armed with. A coordinator identity
that receives mail in more than one project currently gets notified for only one — the rest is
a silent blind spot.

## Background
The monitor polls `am check-inbox --agent <A> --project <CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR>` (src/core/am.ts).
`check-inbox` is single-project: its only scoping flag is `--project` (one key), with no
product/cross-project mode. So the watch sees exactly one project's inbox.

This bit for real. WindyBarn's monitor was armed with
`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/home/gulp/projects/tiny-claude-plugins`, but the entire GrayBrook↔WindyBarn
thread (msgs 27588 / 27589 / the follow-up) lives in the VAULT project
(`/home/gulp/Vaults/everything`). GrayBrook's reply could not reach the monitor — confirmed at
the OS level (running deno pid polls the tiny-claude-plugins project only). The recipient never
gets a "new mail" signal for mail that landed in a project the monitor isn't pinned to.

This is the monitor-side twin of tcp-p0x.1: the same "one identity, many project-ids" friction,
on the WATCH path instead of the LOOKUP path. Both stem from `am`'s per-project scoping.

## Design sketch
- `am` already exposes a cross-project surface: `am robot overview` returns per-project
  unread/urgent/ack COUNTS across projects. Use it as the cheap cross-project detector: poll
  overview for the agent; when any project's unread count rises, drill into THAT project with
  `check-inbox` to fetch the new message details and emit the notification (tagged with which
  project it came from).
- Alternatively/additionally, a product-scoped mode: `am products` links projects into a
  product; MCP has `fetch_inbox_product`. When the identity's projects are a linked product,
  watch the product.
- Config: a monitor option (env, e.g. `MAIL_WATCH_SCOPE=project|all|product` +
  `MAIL_PRODUCT=<key>`), defaulting to today's single-project behavior so nothing regresses.
- Read-only throughout — overview and check-inbox both leave messages unread.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Register one identity (WindyBarn) that receives mail in two projects (A = tiny-claude-plugins,
   B = vault).
2. Arm the monitor with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=A`.
3. Have someone send WindyBarn a message in project B.
4. The monitor never notifies — it polls only A's inbox.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A cross-project (or product-scoped) watch mode emits a notification for a new message in ANY
  of the identity's projects, tagging the source project in the notification line.
- Default behavior (single project) is unchanged when the new mode is not requested.
- Still read-only: no message is marked read by the watch.
- A test covers "message in a non-armed project triggers a notification" (the exact miss above).

## Verification
Reproduce the two-project setup; a message in the non-armed project produces a notification
naming that project; `deno test --allow-write` covers the cross-project detection path.

## Notes
- Pairs with tcp-p0x.1 (global message resolver): together they close the read + watch halves of
  the coordinator-across-project-ids gap.
- Aside observed while diagnosing: a stale 0.3.0 monitor (identity AzureAnchor,
  everything-tooling) is still running the RETIRED scripts/mail-monitor.sh — unrelated leftover,
  reinforces tcp-p0x.3's entrypoint-retirement cleanup.

title: monitor: ack/urgency-aware watch + opt-in ack subscription (robot inbox backing)
description:
## Goal
Make the monitor ack/urgency-aware: (a) tag ack-required (and urgent) messages in the
notification line, and (b) offer an opt-in "subscribe to acks" watch mode that notifies ONLY on
ack-required / ack-overdue mail. Read-only throughout.

## Background
Two asks converge here. Surfacing acks and "subscribing" to acks are the same seam.

The monitor polls `am check-inbox` (src/core/am.ts). Verified against live output: check-inbox's
per-message shape is ONLY `{id, subject, from, importance, created_ts}` — it carries NO ack
field, and check-inbox has no flag to add one. So the notification line
(`MAIL #<id> from <from> [<importance>]: <subject>`, watch.ts:formatLine) literally has no ack
data to render. (An earlier assumption that `ack_required` was "already parsed" was wrong — that
field comes from the `am mail reply` RESPONSE payload, not from check-inbox.)

The ack/urgency data lives in a DIFFERENT command: `am robot inbox` — "Actionable inbox with
priority ordering, urgency/ack synthesis", with `--urgent`, `--ack-overdue`, `--include-bodies`.
That is the natural backing source for both an ack marker AND an ack subscription filter.

## Design sketch
- Add an opt-in mode (env, e.g. `MAIL_WATCH_MODE=basic|actionable`, default `basic` = today's
  check-inbox behavior — no regression).
- In `actionable` mode, poll `am robot inbox --agent A --project P --json` (map its
  `{_meta, inbox:[…]}` envelope), read the per-message urgency/ack fields, and render an ack /
  urgent marker on the notification line, e.g.
  `MAIL #<id> from <from> [<importance>] (ACK-REQUIRED): <subject>`.
- Subscription: expose `--ack-overdue` / `--urgent` pass-throughs (e.g. `MAIL_WATCH_FILTER=
  ack|urgent`) so the watch fires ONLY on ack-required/overdue (or urgent) mail — the
  "subscribe to acks" feature, backed by am's own filters.

## Caveat / decision baked in
`am robot inbox` is the ACTIONABLE (filtered) view: for an already-engaged thread it returns
`count: 0` where `check-inbox` still lists the messages. So it must NOT wholesale-replace
check-inbox as the default — that would silently DROP notifications for mail robot-inbox deems
non-actionable. Keep check-inbox as the default detector; robot-inbox is an opt-in
enrichment/filter mode.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Default (basic) mode is byte-for-byte unchanged (check-inbox, current notification format).
- `actionable` mode tags ack-required / urgent messages in the notification line, sourced from
  `am robot inbox`.
- A filter mode notifies only on ack-required/overdue (and/or urgent) messages —
  the "subscription".
- Still read-only (robot inbox with no mutating flags does not mark read — verify).
- Tests cover: (1) an ack-required message gets the marker; (2) filter mode suppresses a
  non-ack message; (3) basic mode output is unchanged.

## Verification
`deno test --allow-write` covers the three cases above; a live run in a project with an
ack-required message shows the marker (and, in filter mode, only that message).

## Notes
- Sibling of tcp-p0x.6 (cross-project watch): both are "make the watch smarter about which mail
  matters", and a full coordinator watch eventually wants BOTH cross-project scope AND
  ack/urgency awareness.

title: AM broadcast: reconcile flag-works vs robot-docs-says-unsupported drift (report upstream + fix plugin swarm docs)
description:
## Goal
Reconcile a documentation-vs-implementation drift in Agent Mail's broadcast surface, and
record the resolved behavior where the plugin's swarm docs can rely on it. Report the doc
drift upstream (mcp_agent_mail_rust); do NOT change am source.

## Background
Surfaced while researching how the AM server supports swarms (design note
`design/agent-mail-swarm-model-and-robot-surface.md` in the vault). Three sources disagree,
and the disagreement was verified against source:

- **The tool layer supports broadcast.** `send_message` takes `broadcast: Option<bool>`
  (`crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/messaging.rs`). With `broadcast=true` and an empty `to`,
  the server expands `to` to every project agent active in the last 30 days, minus the sender
  and anyone with `contact_policy=block_all` (messaging.rs ~1011-1032). Mutually exclusive with
  an explicit `to`. Unit-tested (messaging.rs ~2567).
- **The pseudo-recipient route is rejected.** Naming an agent `all`/`everyone`/`broadcast`/`*`
  as a recipient errors "Agent Mail doesn't support broadcasting to all agents"
  (`BROADCAST_TOKENS` / `looks_like_broadcast`, `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/models.rs`) —
  that error's job is to steer callers to the flag.
- **The agent-facing guide disclaims it.** `am robot-docs guide` (Coordination Safety) says
  "Broadcast send_message is intentionally unsupported."

Net: the flag works; the guide is stale/conservative relative to it. A caller that wants
fan-out today (e.g. agent-mail-coordinator's `amc broadcast`) implements N individual sends
client-side because the guide told it broadcast was unsupported.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT modify am / mcp_agent_mail_rust source — the flag behavior is correct as-is.
- Not a plugin code change; this is a knowledge-reconciliation + upstream-report task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The drift is reported upstream (issue/note against mcp_agent_mail_rust: the `robot-docs guide`
  "broadcast intentionally unsupported" line contradicts the working, tested `broadcast` flag) —
  link or reference recorded here.
- The plugin's swarm docs (e.g. `driving-swarms-with-mail`) either (a) note the working
  `broadcast=true`+empty-`to` fan-out with the 30-day/active/not-block_all recipient rule, or
  (b) explicitly defer to the reconciled upstream doc — no plugin doc should repeat the stale
  "unsupported" claim as fact.

## Verification
Re-run `am robot-docs guide` after any upstream fix lands to confirm the line is reconciled; a
live `send_message(broadcast=true, to=[])` in a multi-agent project fans out to the eligible
set (read-only to confirm: check recipients on the resulting message).

## Notes
Grounded in the vault design note; citations are greppable file refs against
~/projects/mcp_agent_mail_rust, not frozen line numbers.

title: am robot atc + handoff: probe and document the two undocumented subcommands
description:
## Goal
Probe and document the two `am robot` subcommands that have zero prose anywhere — `atc` and
`handoff` — so the plugin's swarm/coordinator docs can reference them by behavior, not just by
one-line synopsis.

## Background
Surfaced by the `am robot` surface Rumsfeld-quadrant pass (vault design note
`design/agent-mail-swarm-model-and-robot-surface.md`). Both subcommands **postdate the am
repo's own `docs/SPEC-script-migration-matrix.md`** and carry no "when to use" prose in any
skill, spec, or vault note — only their `--help` flags:

- **`robot atc`** — "ATC snapshot: live server state with local DB fallback when unavailable."
  Synopsis suggests an operator/liveness surface (the "ATC" = air-traffic-control metaphor).
  Unknown: what it returns, how the local-DB fallback manifests, whether it's read-only.
- **`robot handoff`** — "Stale bead ownership handoff dashboard with dry-run reopen
  recommendations" (`--stale-minutes --active-minutes --fresh-comment-minutes`). This is the one
  robot subcommand whose synopsis directly gestures at swarm hygiene (detecting abandoned worker
  ownership) — directly relevant to the coordinator loop — yet is entirely undocumented.

## Non-goals
- Not an am source change; this is discovery + documentation.
- Do not act on `handoff --dry-run` reopen recommendations against live beads until the
  command's semantics are confirmed safe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `atc` and `handoff` each get a short "what it returns / when to use / read-only?" note,
  sourced from a live `--json` probe (and, where cheap, a source read of the am crate).
- `handoff`'s relevance to the coordinator loop is captured where the swarm docs live
  (e.g. `driving-swarms-with-mail` or a coordinator skill) — at minimum, that it exists and
  surfaces stale bead ownership with a dry-run reopen preview.
- The Rumsfeld note's "known unknowns" entry for atc/handoff is updated to "known knowns" once
  characterized.

## Verification
`am robot atc --json` and `am robot handoff --json --dry-run` run cleanly and their output shape
is recorded; a re-read of the design note reflects the promotion from unknown to characterized.

## Finding (2026-07-24 probe) — `atc` partially characterized
Live `am robot atc --json` on the installed 0.3.21 base build returns
`{"enabled": false, "source": "disabled", "note": "ATC is disabled by configuration."}` with
`_actions: ["Start the local server for live ATC state: am serve-http"]`. Cause: the systemd unit
sets `AM_ATC_ENABLED=false` (the ATC *adaptive-learning sidecar* — `atc.sqlite3` — is
non-functional in base-mode; schema never created). So on this machine `robot atc` is **not** a
general server-liveness probe — it reports the ATC subsystem's own (disabled) state. **Still
open:** what `robot atc` returns with ATC *enabled*, and `robot handoff` (fully unprobed).

Corollary surfaced same probe: the reliable local-DB liveness read is **`robot status`** (returns
instantly even when the HTTP server is wedged and `am status` hangs) — captured in the wedge
diagnosis (beads `tcp-p0x.10` diagnosis skill, `tcp-p0x.11` systemd watchdog). Design note
`design/agent-mail-swarm-model-and-robot-surface.md` updated: `atc` moved from known-unknown to
partially-characterized.

## Notes
Pairs with b-f8 (broadcast drift) — both are AM-surface findings from the same research pass,
filed so today's synthesis doesn't evaporate before it's actioned.
